limitations: Corpus tokenization does not prove atomic lexicality.
POS tags are evidence signals, not final Cantonese lexical categories.
Proper-name and domain-concentration signals trigger review, not automatic exclusion.
A valid rare/formal/archaic Cantonese lexeme may remain outside the final common 2,000 without being removed from the broader runtime lexicon.
Cifu definitions/Jyutping and Rime weights do not determine final inclusion.
Protected #796 ranks 1001-1250 require separate handling and are not directly adjudicated by this candidate generator.
purpose: Expanded direct-spoken surface candidate pool for expert curation/backfill to exactly 2,000 genuine common Cantonese lexical items.

ranking.cross_corpus_balance: min(corpus ppm) / max(corpus ppm); 1 is balanced and 0 is single-corpus
ranking.filter: surface contains at least one Han ideograph; punctuation/Latin-only tokens excluded
ranking.score: arithmetic mean of HKCanCor ppm and CantoMap ppm (equal corpus weight)
ranking.tie_break: both-corpora attestation, pooled raw count, Unicode surface order

signals.domain_concentration_review: cross-corpus balance below 0.10; not an automatic exclusion
signals.hkcancor_proper_like_share: share of HKCanCor raw tags in conservative nr/ns/nt/nz proper-name families; review signal only
signals.known_invalid_atomic: surface appears in expert-adjudicated invalid-atom retirement ledgers; does not count as a lexical-core item
signals.pos: raw corpus POS distributions; curation signal only

cifu_secondary.role: secondary historical rank/frequency and candidate-reading comparison only

invalid_atomic_ledgers.role: prior expert lexicality exclusions; frequency/regression not used as deletion criteria

cantomap.pos_role: PyCantonese conversion/tagging signal; lower evidentiary weight than direct HKCanCor annotation

hkcancor.pos_role: original HKCanCor annotation where present; evidence, not final ontology
